Shri Shreyash Pandit - Advocate for respondent No.4.
 Order

This petition under Article 226 22 of Constitution of India has been filed against order dated 18.07.2017 passed by Collector, Rewa in case No.14/A-74/Original/2015 74/Original/2015-16 16 by which application filed by petitioner under Section 28-A A (1 and 2) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been rejected on the ground that petitioner is not a similarly situated person.

2. It is submitted by counsel for petitioner that in fact Collector, Rewa should have directed for inquiry to find out as to whether the case of petitioner is at par with the case of one Shri Vishram Prasad Tiwari in whose case the compensation amount was enhanced by Court under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
3. Per contra, the petition is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State.

By referring to the the application filed under Section 28 28-A of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, 1894 it is submitted by counsel for respondents that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:54218 2024:MPHC petitioner had not pointed out as to how his case is similar to the case of Vishram Prasad Tiwari.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text:
1 5. Section 28-A A of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 reads as under:
"28A. Re-determination determination of the amount of compensation on the basis of the award of the ourt.- (1)

Where in an award under this Part, Court the Court ourt allows to the applicant any amount of compensation in excess of the amount awarded byy the Collector under section 11,11, the persons interested in all the other land covered by the same notification under section 4, sub-section section (1) and who are also aggrieved by the award of the Collector may, notwithstanding that they had not made an application to the Collector under section 18, by written application to the Collector within three months from the date of the award of the Court Court require that the amount of compensation payable to them may be re re- determined on the basis of the amount of compensation awarded by the Court;

C Provided that in computing the period of three months within which an application to the Collector shall be made under thist sub-section section, the day on which the award was pronounced and the time requisite for obtaining a copy of the award shall be excluded.

ex (2) The Collector shall, on receipt of an application under sub-section sub (1), ),
conduct an inquiry after giving notice to all the persons interested and giving giv them a reasonable opportunity of being heard and make an award determining the amount of compensation payable to the applicants.

(3) Any person who has not accepted the award under sub-section sub section (2)
may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector Collector for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:54218 2024:MPHC determination of the Court Court and the provisions of sections 18 to 28 shall, so far as may be, apply to such reference as they apply to a reference under section 18."

6. From plain reading of the aforesaid Section, it is clear that if the Court has awarded an additional compensation to a person person, then all other persons interested in all other land covered by same notification and are also aggrieved by the same award passed by the Collector and notwithstanding as to whether they had made any application under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 or not

,
they are also entitled for re-determination determination of the amount of compensation on the basis of the award of the Court.

7. The Collector, Rewa has considered the aspect and has held that the Court while enhancing the compensation amount in the case of Vishram Prasad Tiwari had observed that opportunity of hearing was not given to Vishram Prasad Tiwari prior to passing of award and no spot inspection was carried out as to whether the land in dispute was irrigated land and was yielding two crops and no valuation of tube- well\/well /well was done and the objection objection raised by the applicant applicant/petitioner as well as the evidence was not taken into consideration.

However, in the application filed under Section 28-A 28 A of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 1894, petitioner has not Rajkumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81109628/
2 claimed that his case is similarly situated to the case of Vishram Prasad Tiwari.

sentences.text: If petitioner was not having any tube tube-well/well or his land was un--irrigated irrigated land and was yielding only one crop, then he would not be entitled to the benefit of the reasoning assigned by the Court while enhancing the compensation awarded awarded to Vishram Prasad Tiwari.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:54218 2024:MPHC 8.

It is submitted by counsel for petitioner that in paragraph 13 of the award dated 29.10.2015 passed by trial Court in the case of Vishram Prasad Tiwari, it was held that since the land was acquired for industrial purposes, es, therefore, he is entitled for 1 and 1/2 times of the market value.

9. The aforesaid submission made by counsel for petitioner may be right but it is misconceived so far as the facts of present case are concerned.
10. The basic question is that what is the market value of the property belonging to petitioner,
petitioner which was acquired by the State for the benefit of respondent No.4?
11.

Since the trial Court while deciding the Reference Reference made by Vishram Prasad Tiwari came to a conclusion with regard to the nature of property i.e. irrigated and yielding two crops with tube well/well and no such pleadings have been made in the application filed under Section 28-A A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, therefore, the market value of the land of petitioner, petitioner which was acquired cquired cannot be determ determined on the basis of principles, which were taken into consideration by the trial Court.
12.

Faced with a situation, it is submitted by counsel for petitioner that petitioner was not granted 1 and 1/2 time of the mar market value as determined by the trial rial Court in the case of Vishram Prasad Tiwari.
13. However, he fairly conceded that no such pleading was made by petitioner in his application filed under Section 28 28-A of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:54218 2024:MPHC 14.

In absence of any basic pleading, pleading Collector, Rewa did not commit any mistake by rejecting the application filed under Section 28 28-A of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
15.
As no illegality was committed committed by Collector, Rewa, therefore, order dated 18.07.2017 passed by Collector, Rewa in case No. No.14/A- 74/Original/2015-16 16 is hereby affirmed.
16. Petition ition fails and is hereby dismissed.
